red_tests.failure_fingerprint: AttributeError: module has no attribute '_dev_branch_skip_provenance' — the branch guard does not exist in scripts/test_provenance_guard.py at this baseline

correction_reason: ruff F821: the fake _git stub annotated its return as subprocess.CompletedProcess while importing subprocess inside the function body, so the annotation forward-referenced a name not bound at module scope. Import moved to the top of the file. Found by the Code Quality and Security Audit check on PR #123, not by inspection: CI runs ruff with --select E9,F63,F7,F82 over project/ and tests/, and F821 is in that set. The test content and its 21 assertions are otherwise unchanged.
rationale: The pre-rebase-kan214-wip stash added a branch-aware provenance guard but never called _dev_branch_skip_provenance, so it was dead code no test could see. This pins the behaviour the feature claims, and pins the fail-closed default for any branch name not on the allowlist: a soft-guard keyed on 'anything that is not main' would let a typo'd branch name skip the gate. The patterns are asserted against the guard's own module constants, imported by path, so deleting the constants in the source fails these tests rather than leaving a stale copy here to pass against.
